::: {#brief .lx-sec}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-cap-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The brief</p>
<p class="lx-case-q">Design, carry out and report a study of your own at one scale: a question you chose, a method you can defend, and a result someone else can rerun.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">The course's research capstone. It certifies nothing; it gives you the evidence a mentor needs to judge whether you are ready for supervised research.</p>
<ol class="lx-studio-task">
<li><b>Hand in:</b> a one-page proposal, a reproducible repository (or an audit trail for qualitative work), a six-page paper, a poster and your rubric sheet.</li>
<li><b>From:</b> a question card from the <a href="r10-question-studio.html">question studio</a>, one scale route (its model lab and capstone), the research studios and <a href="ck-m-unseen-problem.html">CK-M</a>.</li>
<li><b>Done when:</b> every stage below meets its own check, <a href="ck-r-defend-revise.html">CK-R</a>'s mock review is answered, and your self-check reaches Proficient on every competence.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">About 20 to 40 hours of your own work, CK-R's four among them: about an hour on this page, then the study. A mentor's review and a peer-review swap are optional, and help most.</p>
</div>

<div class="lx-card cr-tracks-card">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Three tracks, one rubric</p>
<!-- cr-tracks:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="cr-tracks"><div class="cr-track"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Model-based</p><p><b>Optimization or simulation.</b> A model of the system that answers what to do, or what would happen.</p><dl class="cr-dl"><div><dt>Questions</dt><dd>Prescriptive, predictive or explanatory</dd></div><div><dt>Rerun</dt><dd>Reruns from a <span class="lx-term" data-term="clean-clone">clean clone</span>; checked against a hand calculation or a published benchmark, and validated against real data.</dd></div><div><dt>Lessons</dt><dd><a href="m01-dispatch-to-lmp.html">M1</a>, <a href="m03-capacity-expansion.html">M3</a>, <a href="b03-read-check-formulation.html">B3</a></dd></div></dl></div><div class="cr-track"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Empirical</p><p><b>Data analysis, or a reproduction or replication of a published result.</b> An analysis of observed data; or a published result rerun with its own data and code (a computational reproduction), or tested on new data (a replication).</p><dl class="cr-dl"><div><dt>Questions</dt><dd>Descriptive, explanatory, evaluative or predictive</dd></div><div><dt>Rerun</dt><dd>Reruns from a clean clone, raw data to result; a reproduction or a replication reports how close it came to the published number.</dd></div><div><dt>Lessons</dt><dd><a href="b02-python-data.html">B2</a>, <a href="m14-did-it-work.html">M14</a>, <a href="r04-data.html">R4</a></dd></div></dl></div><div class="cr-track"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Mixed</p><p><b>A model or data analysis with a stakeholder or qualitative part.</b> Numbers and people's reasons, with a plan for how each informs the other.</p><dl class="cr-dl"><div><dt>Questions</dt><dd>Explanatory, evaluative or prescriptive</dd></div><div><dt>Rerun</dt><dd>A clean-clone rerun for the numbers; an audit trail from raw notes to themes for the qualitative part.</dd></div><div><dt>Lessons</dt><dd><a href="r09-integrity-stakeholders.html">R9</a>, <a href="a13-fairness-jobs.html">A13</a>, <a href="r03-system-and-method.html">R3</a></dd></div></dl></div></div>
<!-- cr-tracks:end -->
<p class="lx-hint">Every track is judged on the same nine competences. A fully qualitative study is allowed with a mentor; the course teaches qualitative methods at awareness level only.</p>
<details class="lx-textalt cr-routes"><summary>The five scale routes: a model lab and a capstone each</summary>
<!-- cr-routes:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<table class="lx-facts cr-routes-t"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Scale</th><th scope="col">Model lab</th><th scope="col">Capstone</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>S0 device and plant</td><td>M4</td><td>C0</td></tr><tr><td>S1 microgrid and community</td><td>M5</td><td>C1</td></tr><tr><td>S2 regional grid</td><td>M2</td><td>C2</td></tr><tr><td>S3 city and region</td><td>M12</td><td>C3</td></tr><tr><td>S4 nation</td><td>M13</td><td>C4</td></tr></tbody></table>
<!-- cr-routes:end -->
</details>
</div>
```

## Write your one-page proposal
:::

```{=html}
<div id="cr-note" class="cr-note">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- cr-note:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<ol class="lx-rn-outline"><li><b>Title and plan link:</b> the plan's link from the planner above, and the date</li><li><b>Why it matters:</b> Who would act on the answer, and what answer would change their decision.</li><li><b>The plan:</b> your question card's eight parts; the track, the scale route, the method and its alternatives, the mock review, the time and the milestones</li><li><b>Assumptions:</b> the hours a week the weeks rest on</li><li><b>Sensitivity:</b> the uncertainty treatment you plan</li><li><b>What is known, and the gap:</b> The three closest studies and what none of them answers; the size of your concept matrix and the date of your search (R2).</li><li><b>Why this method, not the alternatives:</b> What your method answers that the two alternatives cannot (if one is from your method's family, name that method exactly), and one limit you will mitigate (R3).</li><li><b>Data and licences:</b> Each source, its date and its licence; for interviews, who you will ask, how you will ask for consent, and the ethics review you need first (R4, R9).</li><li><b>How you will check it:</b> One verification check, one validation against real data or an independent reference, and the tolerance you set now (R5).</li><li><b>What the study leaves out:</b> The parts, people and years outside your boundary, and why that does not change the answer to your question.</li><li><b>Integrity:</b> Credit, conflicts, consent, and who the study affects (R9).</li></ol>
<!-- cr-note:end -->
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, your question card and your plan fill in the proposal's table, and the checks say which parts are in place. Without it, write the proposal under these headings, on one page.</p>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Researcher</span>A mentor's review and the peer-review swap</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **A mentor** reads three things: the proposal, the validation evidence and the final study. Send each with its rubric self-rating.
- **The swap:** two learners exchange proposals and review each other's with [CK-R](ck-r-defend-revise.html)'s review form, within a week; then answer point by point, and swap again for the paper's draft.
- **The reviewer's duties:** keep the other proposal confidential, do not use its ideas without permission, and declare any conflict (ALLEA 2023, §2.8).
- **Credit:** name your reviewers in the paper's acknowledgements.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-ex-cols">

[1]</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Falls short:</b> No type, no audience, no metric, no comparison: nobody could say when it is answered.</li></ol></div>
<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Strong · Strong</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Question:</b> Did homes weatherized in 2023 cut their gas use [1] over the next two winters by more than similar homes still on the waiting list? [2]
<b>Type:</b> evaluative.
<b>Audience:</b> the city's housing office, which sets next year's budget and would cut the programme if the saving is under 5%. [3]
<b>Metric:</b> the change in winter gas use per home, two winters before against two after, kWh, adjusted for the weather.
<b>Scale:</b> S3; boundary: the homes' gas, not their electricity.
Wrong if: the waiting-list homes' use fell as much. [4]
Selection: homes that waited may differ; I compare their use before 2023 too. [5]</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Works:</b> A metric; its units follow.</li><li value="2"><b>Works:</b> A candidate comparison group: homes that applied too, assumed alike apart from the work. It stands in for the counterfactual.</li><li value="3"><b>Works:</b> Who acts on the answer, and the answer that would change the decision.</li><li value="4"><b>Works:</b> A falsification statement, on the same change.</li><li value="5"><b>Works:</b> The comparison's main weakness, named, with a check.</li></ol></div>
</div></div>
<div class="cr-ex-static"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Positioning: the gap</p><p class="lx-hint">Stage 2, literature · Prairie City's 2023 <span class="lx-term" data-term="weatherization">weatherization</span> programme: did weatherized homes use less gas than homes on its waiting list (empirical, evaluative, S3).</p><p class="lx-hint"><b>Task:</b> State what is known and the gap.</p><p class="lx-hint">Both fragments are illustrative; the study is fictional and its numbers are assumed, not computed.</p>
<div class="lx-ex-cols">

<div class="lx-ex-ans good"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Strong · Strong</p><p class="lx-ex-lines"><b>Known:</b> of the 14 studies in my concept matrix, 9 use billing data and 3 compare with a waiting list; [1] none of the 3 is in a city with winters this cold. [2]

[4]</p><ol class="lx-ex-static"><li value="1"><b>Works:</b> The map behind the claim: a matrix of more than 12 sources.</li><li value="2"><b>Works:</b> The empty cell, stated precisely.</li><li value="3"><b>Works:</b> A dated search a reviewer can repeat.</li><li value="4"><b>Works:</b> The closest prior work, engaged directly.</li></ol></div>
</div></div>

<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts lx-rb-static"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Competence</th><th scope="col">Developing</th><th scope="col">Proficient (the bar)</th><th scope="col">Strong</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Framing<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: Your proposal's question card passes its eight checks and says what answer would change your audience's decision.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Question vague or untyped; no audience or counterfactual.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Typed question with audience or decision-maker, metric with units, counterfactual, scale and boundary; one falsification statement.</td><td data-l="Strong">Also explains why the question matters to its audience and what answer would change a decision.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Positioning<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: Your concept matrix of 12 sources or more, and a dated search behind the gap.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">A few sources, no map.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Concept matrix of at least 12 sources; a stated gap with evidence.</td><td data-l="Strong">The gap survives a search by a reviewer; closest prior work engaged directly.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Method fit<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: Your method defended against the two alternatives in your plan, and one limit you mitigated.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Method chosen by habit.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Method defended against two alternatives, one of them a different family.</td><td data-l="Strong">Limits of the chosen method stated and partly mitigated.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Trustworthy analysis<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: A clean-clone rerun (CK-R), a verification log and one validation, named in the paper.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Results cannot be rerun.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Reruns from a clean clone (or a complete audit trail); verification log; one validation against real data or an independent reference.</td><td data-l="Strong">Independent reproduction by someone else; validation on data not used to build the analysis.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Uncertainty<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: The main result as a range, with how the range was made.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Single numbers.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Uncertainties classified; scenario or global sensitivity analysis; results as ranges.</td><td data-l="Strong">Decision-relevant uncertainty identified and its value discussed.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Consistent accounting<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: Cost and emissions on one boundary where you report them, the emissions question named, and who pays and who benefits.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Costs and emissions on different boundaries.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Cost and emissions on one boundary; emissions question named; who pays and who benefits named.</td><td data-l="Strong">Distributional and environmental side effects estimated with stated assumptions.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Realism<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: The evidence status of your key inputs, and a list of what the study leaves out.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Assumes announced projects exist.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Evidence status of key inputs; a 'what the analysis leaves out' list.</td><td data-l="Strong">Realism checked with a practitioner or primary documents.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Communication<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: The six-page paper, its key figure, the limits paragraph and the 150-word public summary.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Results without limits.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Six-page paper; one key figure; a limits paragraph; a 150-word public summary.</td><td data-l="Strong">A briefing a decision-maker could act on without misreading.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Integrity<br><span class="lx-hint">Look for: Your integrity statement: licences, credit, conflicts and consent; what you released.</span></th><td data-l="Developing">Licences or credit unchecked.</td><td data-l="Proficient">Licences checked, credit and conflicts stated, stakeholders treated fairly.</td><td data-l="Strong">Data and code released with documentation where allowed.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<!-- cr-rubric:end -->
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-xcard">
<header class="lx-x-head"><h3>Two statuses you can claim, in your own words</h3></header>
<!-- cr-statuses:start (written from the data file by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-scroll-x"><table class="lx-facts cr-status-t"><thead><tr><th scope="col">Status</th><th scope="col">Requires</th><th scope="col">Evidence you can show</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Completed Research Studio</th><td data-l="Requires">The core path, the checkpoints CK-F, CK-A and CK-M, and a submitted CR with a self-assessment.</td><td data-l="Evidence">The CR repository and report, the rubric sheet.</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Demonstrated supervised-project readiness at scale Sx</th><td data-l="Requires">The above, plus the Sx route, CK-R, and Proficient or better on all nine rubric competences. A mentor's review of the proposal, the validation evidence and the final study is optional but recommended.</td><td data-l="Evidence">The same, plus the CK-R review and response, and the mentor's comments if any.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<!-- cr-statuses:end -->
<p class="lx-hint">The course issues no certificate or badge. A web course cannot verify who did the work or replace a mentor's judgement: it gives you a published standard and the evidence to show against it.</p>
</div>
</div>
```
